segments.title: Chương 58: 0058【Danh Văn Xuất, Danh Hiệu Tranh Giành】
segments.content:
(The manuscript has been revised, so let's just publish this chapter. That's all for today, will update on time tomorrow.)

The editor is not being helpful, can't even run interference for the author. Hearing that a masterpiece had appeared, everyone flocked over to spectate.

Reading the preliminary round essays just now had been too agonizing for them; now, they needed to cleanse their eyes properly.

Seeing too many people surging forward, and not being able to afford to offend any of them, Hu Weishi had a stroke of genius and said, "Why don't we present it to Old Wang to look over first?"

As soon as she said this, no one argued anymore.

Hu Weishi quickly took the final round essay over, placing Chen Guiliang's on the very top.

Wang Meng chuckled and put on his glasses. "I'd like to see for myself just what kind of masterpiece this is."

He lowered his head, leaning close to the essay answer sheet, and was stunned from the very first glance.

Ge Fei asked curiously, "Old Wang, how about I read it aloud?"

"A literary prodigy!"

Wang Meng exclaimed with emotion, then stood up holding the essay. "I'd better read it to you all."

A Journey to Yinghai

In the winter of the Guǐwèi year, I arrived in Shanghai and, inspired by an allegory, wrote of its principles.

It is said that in ancient times, the bird Jingwei carried tiny twigs to fill the vast sea, and the Foolish Old Man chipped at rocks and soil to move great mountains. Looking between heaven and earth, one sees that the most minuscule can achieve the greatest of feats, and the simplest often bears the most complex of truths.

Today there is a mysterious bird, frail and weak of body, that beats its fledgling wings, aspiring to cross the great ocean, carrying a dry twig in hopes of traversing the vast waves. Its will is ever more resolute, its actions ever more valiant. Does this not secretly align with the ultimate truth of the universe?

What is this principle? It is to strive ceaselessly for self-improvement!

Our ancestors in Huaxia blazed trails through thorns to open up the forests and mountains, and with united effort, they secured our nation's integrity. The world today is an era of great contention; powerful nations stand like a forest, and all states vie for supremacy. To seek the rejuvenation of our nation, we students have an undeniable duty.

As Zhuangzi once said: "The wren builds its nest in the forest, but uses no more than a single branch." I come from a humble background, possessing nothing of value, yet I hope to use my faint light to illuminate the entire starry river of the galaxy.

I nervously compose these three hundred words of "A Journey to Yinghai," not merely to sing of an object, but also to declare my ambition. With this preface, I hope the reader may understand the true essence of the poem. For within this humble heart, there exists an ambition to prop up heaven and earth!

Toward Yingzhou in the east, what heroic spirit is seen,

A mysterious bird with twig in beak breaks the primordial scene.

Its wings skim past Fusang, thirty thousand leagues away,

Its beak holds a dry cattail from the supreme celestial bay.

In Penglai's shallow waters, the Kun Peng lies in sleep,

In Fangzhang's heavy clouds, the Horned Dragon sorrows deep.

A clear cry from beyond the heavens suddenly resounds,

Straight to the vast sea, it goes, where immortal trace is found.

Its first flight shakes its feathers from the Jade Terrace on high,

The moon's grotto and cold stars cast its shadow from the sky.

Kunlun's snow has melted, ice now serves as its glass,

The Placid Weak Water's waves turn jade to dusty mass.

The fairy of Guye Mountain tosses a jade-flower spray,

The Goddess of the Luo River leaves a pearl she bore that day.

The nine heavens' astral winds tear at its wings and plume,

Yet it clutches the lone twig, refusing to meet its doom.

It falls into the surging waves, a hundred-zhang abyss,

Black waves like mountains hang above, a crushing, dark dismiss.

The jiaoren's weeping pearls become a rain of blood and dread,

The mirage of the sea-serpent dissolves to blue smoke instead.

It soars straight up again, ninety thousand leagues anew,

Weary, it throws the dry twig down, a wild duck's boat in view.

The stars hang upside down within a cup of water's space,

The universe is overturned right before its face.

Where Jingwei once filled the sea, that very ancient ground,

The wood and stone still carry the crying cuckoo's angry sound.

Emperor Qin's grand warships sank beneath the turquoise tides,

Zheng He's giant treasure ships have rotted masts besides.

Through ages, rise and fall have chased the waves that flow and flee,

Only this branch, forever, is carried across the sea.

The people of today are also guests who carry a branch,

Regarding terrifying waves as a simple, grassy branch.

Alas!

Do not say Huaxia has no extraordinary men,

Just watch this humble body unfurl a grand design.

If one day I fulfill my ambition to mend the sky,

I will throw this branch again to fill the great Emptiness!

When Wang Meng finished reading, the entire hall was silent.

Many people were stunned.

Many others hadn't quite understood and wanted to see it for themselves.

Yu Hua couldn't be bothered with decorum. He ran directly to Wang Meng's side, even placing a hand on Wang Meng's shoulder, and craned his neck to see the essay on the paper.

With him taking the lead, Tie Yi, Su Tong, Ma Yuan, Cheng Cun, Ye Xin, Fang Fang, and others also gathered around.

The department heads and professors from the major universities were much more composed, sitting quietly in their seats and waiting.

Wang Meng had just read it aloud once, and now he was reading it silently for a second time.

Combining the preface and the poem, by his second read-through, he had completely understood Chen Guiliang's meaning.

On the third read-through, Wang Meng directly recited the lines he liked:

"'The most minuscule can achieve the greatest of feats, and the simplest often bears the most complex of truths.' These two lines contain profound philosophy!"

"'I come from a humble background, possessing nothing of value, yet I hope to use my faint light to illuminate the entire starry river of the galaxy.' This line perfectly shows the sharp spirit of an impoverished youth!"

"'For within this humble heart, there exists an ambition to prop up heaven and earth.' These two lines are even more incredible, truly earth-shattering. They are the foundation of the entire poem. He wants to be the one who props up heaven and earth!"

"'Its first flight shakes its feathers from the Jade Terrace on high, The moon's grotto and cold stars cast its shadow from the sky. Kunlun's snow has melted, ice now serves as its glass, The Placid Weak Water's waves turn jade to dusty mass. The fairy of Guye Mountain tosses a jade-flower spray, The Goddess of the Luo River leaves a pearl she bore that day. The nine heavens' astral winds tear at its wings and plume, Yet it clutches the lone twig, refusing to meet its doom. It falls into the surging waves, a hundred-zhang abyss, Black waves like mountains hang above, a crushing, dark dismiss. The jiaoren's weeping pearls become a rain of blood and dread, The mirage of the sea-serpent dissolves to blue smoke instead.' Oh my, these lines remind me of the ghost-poet Li He!"

"'Through ages, rise and fall have chased the waves that flow and flee, Only this branch, forever, is carried across the sea. The people of today are also guests who carry a branch, Regarding terrifying waves as a simple, grassy branch.' These four lines are also wonderfully written. The dry twig carried by the bird actually represents the ambition of the Chinese people. Dynastic rises and falls are like passing clouds, only this ambition endures. This contestant, Chen Guiliang, calls himself a 'guest who carries a branch.' He wants to preserve this ambition, viewing the terrifying waves as a flat, open plain."

"'Do not say Huaxia has no extraordinary men, Just watch this humble body unfurl a grand design. If one day I fulfill my ambition to mend the sky, I will throw this branch again to fill the great Emptiness!' Excellent, just too well-written. Never mind that the meter and rhyme scheme are off; this is an old-style poem, it doesn't fuss over such things. Even the ancients wouldn't have been overly critical or nitpicky."

Wang Meng read it for a fourth time before stuffing the paper into Yu Hua's hands. "Take it, you're like a monkey."

Yu Hua also appraised it twice, praising it repeatedly. "This is so fucking good. I couldn't write this, no way. Damn it, first classical prose, now a classical poem. This ancient scholar was reborn without drinking Granny Meng's soup of forgetfulness."

Cheng Cun took it and read it carefully, saying, "He's comparing himself to the mysterious bird. Kunlun Mountain is China. He isn't seeking immortals on Kunlun Mountain, but is instead going to Yingzhou. Is he planning to study abroad in America or Japan?"

Fang Fang said, "That should be it. Seeking immortals overseas means studying abroad. Combined with the preface and the last few lines, he wants to return after completing his studies to serve the country."

Tie Yi nodded. "That interpretation makes sense."

"I don't think so," Ma Yuan said. "Something unexpected must have happened on Kunlun Mountain, or rather, to the entirety of China. Even the Kun Peng and the Horned Dragon are trapped by shallow waters and heavy clouds. These images should be referring to the many disasters of modern China. The line 'secured our nation's integrity' in the preface is clearly referring to the War of Resistance Against Japan."

Fang Fang followed this train of thought. "The jiaoren's tears turning into a rain of blood, the sea-serpent's mirage being shattered by surging waves... could that be an allusion to the humanitarian floods of those years?"

Hearing this, Ma Yuan frowned. He didn't like Fang Fang's interpretation.

How could such a strangely beautiful, impassioned, allegorical old-style poem be filled with all sorts of messy things?

The discussion continued.

No one bothered to review the other contestants' essays. They just sat there, discussing and appraising Chen Guiliang's "A Journey to Yinghai."

This old-style poem and its preface had not only surpassed the level of a high school student, but also that of most writers (limited to classical literature).

It was frightening!

Especially after having just read a pile of trashy preliminary round essays.

The contestants had long since returned to the hotel, and now it was free time. But after dinner, they had to wait by the landline phones in their rooms.

Because tonight, the competition results would be out, and the chief editor of Mengya would call to inform them personally.

This time, the wait was probably going to be a bit long!

The essay was passed to Cao Wenxuan. He said with a smile, "If this essay is included in the New Concept award-winning works anthology, it will probably need annotations, or many middle school students won't understand it. I've compiled language textbooks before, so I'm barely qualified for the task of adding notes."

Two professors pursed their lips, not bothering to argue with Cao Wenxuan. They had compiled language textbooks too.

Soon, Ge Fei had also read it twice and left on the pretext of going to the restroom for a smoke.

Ge Fei was the deputy director of Tsinghua's Chinese Department. In the restroom, he called the director of the Chinese Department. "Director Wang, I want to secure a special recruitment spot."

"New Concept?" Director Wang asked.

"Yes," Ge Fei said. "If possible, I want an exemption from the entrance exam, not just a point reduction for admission."

Director Wang said, "Absolutely impossible. The spots have long been set and distributed to major key high schools across the country. We can't even squeeze out half a spot now."

Ge Fei said, "The professors from the various universities are meeting the award-winning contestants tonight. Once they've made their arrangements, it will be very difficult for us to poach anyone!"

After the list of winners was released tonight, the first-prize winners would get a call and then go meet the professors who had recruitment spots.

Mutual communication, a two-way selection.

In principle, one contestant could choose multiple famous universities.

But in practice, that was impossible. They still had to take the independent recruitment exam in March. The exam dates for each university were close, so if a contestant took one, it would be very difficult to take another.

Even after passing the independent recruitment exam, the spot wasn't guaranteed to anyone, because their Gaokao score still had to meet the admission threshold.

For example, if someone applied to Fudan, they would definitely be admitted with a point reduction. But if they wanted to try for Peking University, and passed the independent recruitment exam but their Gaokao score didn't meet Peking University's reduced threshold, they could end up with nothing, admitted by neither Peking University nor Fudan.

"What kind of contestant are you so keen on?" Director Wang asked.

Ge Fei said, "The esteemed Old Wang personally read the essay aloud and publicly analyzed it three or four times. Cao Wenxuan said that when this essay is anthologized, he'll personally write the annotations for the poem. Yu Hua shouted 'fucking good' on the spot and said the contestant was an ancient scholar who was reborn without drinking Granny Meng's soup of forgetfulness."

Director Wang muttered, "You've almost got me convinced."

"In any case, if I were asked to write that essay on the spot, I definitely couldn't do it," Ge Fei said. "If you let me go home with a stack of reference books, I might be able to write something, but it probably wouldn't be as brilliant as his."

"Hold on, I'll make a call and ask." Director Wang was persuaded.

Just as he hung up, Cao Wenxuan suddenly walked in.

The two looked at each other and smiled, both knowing what the other was up to.

Even with a point reduction, the admission thresholds for Tsinghua and Peking University were terrifyingly high. It was very likely they would lose that contestant.

Ignoring the Gaokao and granting an exam-exempt admission was the only safe bet!

"Hello, Head Cheng," Cao Wenxuan dialed a number. "It's like this, I need an exam-exempt special recruitment spot… Yes, New Concept… This contestant is different, an absolute once-in-a-generation talent. If we recruit him, it'll be an achievement for us, and public opinion will surely be full of praise…"

Over the past few years, Old Cao had been using Mengya and New Concept to repeatedly build his presence among students and parents, making a fortune.

He was eager to find another student who could generate buzz, preferably one who could be recruited directly into Peking University!

Ge Fei lingered in the restroom, openly eavesdropping on Cao Wenxuan's phone call.

Before Cao Wenxuan's call was even finished, Director Wang from Tsinghua called back.

"Director Wang, is there a chance?" Ge Fei asked.

Director Wang said, "It's a settled matter; it's impossible to change it at the last minute. Even if we were to change it, we'd have to organize meetings and discuss it repeatedly before it could be approved. Forget it. It's just a student who writes well; there's no need to go to such lengths."

Ge Fei asked, "Can't we really fight for it a little more?"

"I'm hanging up," Director Wang said.

"Sigh, goodbye." Ge Fei was quite helpless.

Cao Wenxuan was still on his call over there. "Right, right… Okay, okay… I'll secure him first. When can a meeting be held to discuss this… After the semester starts? He'll have been snatched up long before then!"

On Peking University's side, if they held a meeting to discuss it, they might actually grant an exam-exempt spot.

They were very flexible.

Last year, they had two New Concept contestants who successfully passed the independent recruitment exam. One was a top student who could have been admitted without any point reduction. The other needed a 30-point reduction to get in, but Peking University had initially set it at 20 points. After a few meetings, they recruited him anyway.

After Cao Wenxuan hung up, Ge Fei walked over and offered him a cigarette. "How are things on your end at Peking University?"

"No problem at all," Cao Wenxuan bluffed.

Ge Fei just smiled.

It didn't matter to him anyway. Since the leadership at Tsinghua didn't agree, he didn't need to think about how to poach the student anymore.

Just then, another professor came in. It was Director Chen from Fudan University's Chinese Department.

Cao Wenxuan thought to himself, it's over.

Last year, Fudan's independent recruitment spots were so tight, yet they still gave point reductions to recruit five New Concept first-prize winners. This year, encountering such a literary genius, they could probably apply for an exam-exempt special recruitment spot!

—
